scope: Local native organization engine and store service; no routes, live gameplay or deployment

checks.name: Release app and Workspace Worker dry build

operations.outcome: Initial focused runs identified two invalid test fixtures: an external task ID and absent projection null defaults. Both fixtures were corrected.
Initial full Workspace run reported fetch failed in the unchanged spell epoch test, with 310 passing checks. The exact isolated test passed; full requalification passed all 311 checks.

acceptance_evidence: Fifteen independently hashed create/update/archive commands accept all metadata kinds in Application and the pinned Workers runtime while preserving unrelated task order/state, history, mappings and game journals.

Exact nonarchived references, partial edits, category set/clear, immutable section membership, complete bounded Todo goal replacement and omitted legacy sets remain enforced. Archival never cascades to tasks or related metadata.

Retained exact command identity recovers the original receipt after later edits, archival or ownership freeze; changed intent and task-command ID collisions fail. Invalid/foreign/stale references and local frozen/cloud authority cannot save.

Account-bound optimistic stores atomically persist metadata plus native receipts. Conflicts and lost acknowledgements recover the original command; failures remain unknown and cancellation propagates.
A synthetic D1 store verifies concurrent compare-and-swap, aborting update failure and lost acknowledgement with one native receipt and no gameplay entries.
limitations: Organization browser/MCP adapters, explicit authorization scope, production controls and actual host qualification remain separate.
The D1 store is an isolated qualification fixture; no public route or production D1 adapter is supplied by the engine.
